source: Project team. Short codes, one-line prompt definitions and triage descriptions for the registry v2 features; paraphrased, not APA text. The registry content (items, features, rules) is unchanged.

features.line: low, sad, empty or hopeless mood most of the day
triage: feeling sad, low, down or depressed
feeling empty or crying a lot
how has your mood been

features.line: clearly less interest or enjoyment in usual activities (not just no chance to do them)
triage: lost interest in things I used to enjoy
nothing feels fun or enjoyable any more

features.line: appetite clearly lower or higher, or weight change without dieting; v decreased or increased
triage: eating less, skipping meals, no appetite
lost or gained weight
how is your appetite

features.line: sleeping too little or too much, with poor rest; v insomnia or hypersomnia
triage: cannot sleep, lying awake at night
sleeping too much all day
how have you been sleeping

features.line: movement or speech visibly slowed or agitated, noticed by others or seen by the clinician; v slowed or agitated
triage: speaking or moving very slowly
others noticed I am slow or restless and fidgety

features.line: tiredness or loss of energy most days
triage: always tired, no energy
exhausted, drained, hard to get out of bed

features.line: feeling worthless, or excessive or misplaced guilt (more than ordinary self-criticism)
triage: I feel worthless, useless, a failure
I feel guilty all the time
everything is my fault

features.line: low opinion of oneself, without excessive guilt
triage: I am not good enough, low confidence
I don't like myself

features.line: no hope that things will improve
triage: nothing will ever get better, hopeless
no point, no future

features.line: trouble thinking, concentrating or deciding; c says what it is linked to
triage: cannot concentrate or focus
hard to make decisions, mind goes blank

features.line: a distinct period of unusually high, euphoric or expansive mood
triage: felt extremely happy, high or on top of the world for days
have you ever had a period of feeling really high
never felt unusually high

features.line: a distinct period of unusually irritable mood with raised energy
triage: a period of being very irritable and full of energy
snapping at everyone for days while wired

features.line: persistently raised energy or activity during a distinct period
triage: had loads of energy, could not stop
unusually energetic and active for days

features.line: inflated self-esteem or grandiose beliefs
triage: felt special, powerful, better than everyone
believed I had special abilities

features.line: needing much less sleep yet feeling rested (not insomnia with tiredness)
triage: slept only a few hours and still felt full of energy
did not need sleep

features.line: talking much more than usual or pressure to keep talking
triage: talking nonstop, people could not interrupt
much more talkative than usual

features.line: thoughts racing or jumping between ideas
triage: thoughts racing, jumping from idea to idea
mind going too fast

features.line: attention pulled away by unimportant things during a high period
triage: easily distracted by everything during that high time

features.line: big increase in projects or activity, or aimless agitation, during a high period
triage: started many projects at once
doing far more than usual, very busy

features.line: risky activity with painful consequences, such as spending sprees
triage: spent a lot of money impulsively
reckless risky decisions

features.line: admitted to hospital for a high or irritable period
triage: was admitted to hospital
hospitalised because of my behaviour

features.line: hallucinations or delusional beliefs
triage: hearing voices or seeing things others cannot
believing people are plotting against me

features.line: others commented on a mood or behaviour change during a high period
triage: people said I was acting differently, not myself

features.line: an unmistakable change in functioning during a high period
triage: during that time I behaved completely unlike myself

features.line: excessive worry about several areas of life, more days than not
triage: I worry about everything all the time
constant worry about many things
are you a worrier

features.line: hard to stop or control the worrying
triage: cannot stop worrying, cannot control it

features.line: feeling keyed up, tense or on edge
triage: feeling tense, nervous, on edge
anxious and keyed up

features.line: feeling restless or unable to sit still (felt, not only seen)
triage: restless, cannot sit still

features.line: muscle tension, aches or tightness
triage: tight shoulders, tense muscles, aches

features.line: easily annoyed or irritable as an ongoing state; c says what it is linked to
triage: easily annoyed, irritable, snapping at people

features.line: trouble falling or staying asleep, or restless sleep, tied to worry
triage: cannot sleep because I keep worrying
mind will not switch off at night

features.line: fearing that something terrible will happen
triage: afraid something awful will happen
dread something bad is coming

features.line: feeling one might lose control of oneself
triage: afraid I will lose control of myself

features.line: fear, anxiety or embarrassment where others might watch or judge (avoidance alone is not this)
triage: scared of what people think of me
anxious when people are watching me
it's not that I'm scared of people

features.line: fear of acting or showing anxiety in ways others will judge badly
triage: afraid I will embarrass myself
worried people will judge or laugh at me

features.line: feared social situations almost always cause fear
triage: every time I am around people I get anxious

features.line: avoiding social situations or enduring them with distress; c says why (s social fear, m low mood or tiredness)
triage: I avoid friends and stay alone
don't want to go out or talk to people
stopped meeting friends

features.line: social fear clearly larger than the real threat
triage: I know my fear of people is out of proportion

features.line: fear limited to speaking or performing in front of others
triage: afraid of public speaking or presentations
fear only when performing in front of others

features.line: effect on relationships, family, friends or social life; g m marked or c clinically significant
triage: fighting with family, losing friends
my relationships are suffering

features.line: effect on work, study, attendance or performance; g m or c
triage: missing classes or work, grades dropping
cannot do my job or study

features.line: effect on self-care, household or other roles, or significant distress; g m or c
triage: not showering or eating properly, cannot look after myself
it is really distressing

features.line: P only if alcohol, drugs, medication or withdrawal that could cause the symptoms is reported; 'no alcohol or drugs' is D
triage: alcohol, drinking, drugs, smoking, medication
do you use any substances

features.line: P only if an illness that could cause the symptoms is reported; a normal test or no illness is A
triage: thyroid, blood tests, doctor checked me
any medical illness

features.line: P only if a primary psychotic disorder is reported; a cited denial is D
triage: diagnosed with schizophrenia or psychosis

features.line: a recent bereavement or major loss
triage: someone close died recently
a big loss, breakup or bereavement

triage.method: group gating: BM25 on registry queries (generic denial words removed) or E5 similarity to the triage descriptions
triage.measured: Phase 3, 8 dev sessions (role-play + 6 pilot): every group had candidate turns at these thresholds (0 of 40 group calls could be skipped); E5 similarities lie in 0.84-0.92 with no gap between groups with and without reference findings, and E5 costs 3-15 s per session, so it is off by default.
triage.notes: Thresholds set conservatively on the role-play fixture only (no dev reference runs, user decision 10 Nov 2026). Unlisted rows cost no output tokens, so gating is per group, not per feature (plan §12, Phase 3).
